```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab09", title = "Time series regression 1")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "A TSLM with trend() and season() models:",
  q2 = "The omitted quarter in the seasonal dummies is:",
  q3 = "If residual ACF still spikes every 4 quarters, the regression:",
  q4 = "Did trend+season beat SNAIVE on your hold-out? One sentence, name the metric."
)
```

## What you will do

Trend plus seasonal dummies for Beer. Run the fit in an exercise chunk.

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `fpp3`, `learnr`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.


```{r tslm-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=12}
beer <- aus_production |> filter(!is.na(Beer))
train <- beer |> filter_index(. ~ "2007 Q4")
fit <- train |> model(tslm = TSLM(Beer ~ trend() + season()))
report(fit)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("A deterministic trend and quarterly seasonal means", correct = TRUE),
  answer("An ARIMA airline model"),
  answer("A random walk with drift only"),
  answer("Multiplicative Holt-Winters"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("The baseline season; other quarters are differences from it", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Always Q4, and it is dropped from the data"),
  answer("The trend slope"),
  answer("The error variance"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("Has not absorbed the seasonal dynamics", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Is certainly the best forecast"),
  answer("Should be differenced twice"),
  answer("Has no intercept"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "RMSE or MAPE on the test quarters, versus SNAIVE.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
